title: Creating a map in Unreal Engine 5 using AI-generated models.
author: One_Detective_6143
selftext:
I created this map in Unreal Engine 5 over a 9-hour period. This project served as a test of a production pipeline integrated with AI tools.  
I used Gemini to generate the 2D concepts for the assets and characters, and then used Rodin AI and Tripo AI to generate the 3D models and textures.  
To be clear, this is only a prototype test based on *Sea of Thieves*

replies.author: One_Detective_6143
replies.body:
First of all, thank you for the compliment. Yes, the map is set up as a world. I can walk freely through it and interact with the characters. Basically, the map is not fully optimized, but it also doesn’t have millions of tris. Here are more wireframe details >> [https://imgur.com/a/Cn1x2Qm](https://imgur.com/a/Cn1x2Qm) 

About how I made the houses: if you look at the last image, it’s a 2D concept. Think of it this way I took screenshots of each house and asked Gemini to generate a professional 2D concept. After that, I used the generated image to create the 3D model in Rodin, and finally I passed the model through Blender to remove unused material IDs and phantom vertices.

comments.author: devhhh

replies.author: One_Detective_6143
replies.body: Regarding optimization, the meshes are not fully optimized, but I made all the houses around 6k tris. The base rock and the ground mesh have approximately 8k tris, and each character has around 30k tris. I also created only one master material so that, when generating the material for each item in the map, it is created as a material instance, making it lighter. I’m also using 1024x1024 textures. What I can say is that it’s not 100% optimized, but it’s also not one of those maps with 100k or 500k tris per mesh. I’d say it should run smoothly, especially since the meshes are in quads, so it supports automatic LOD generation without issues.

replies.author: One_Detective_6143
replies.body:
Man, there’s no big secret to it. You use Gemini to generate the 2D concepts. If you want something more realistic, you need to ask for a concept with realistic textures; if you want something more cartoony, just ask for a 2D concept leaning toward a cartoon style.

One important detail: always generate the object you want to turn into 3D without a floor and with a gray background in the image. This helps the AI identify the model more accurately and recreate it properly.

If the 3D AI result doesn’t come out well, you can ask the AI to generate multiple angles of the same object and then use a 3D scanning system. After that, you just need to optimize the model using ZRemesh in Blender.

To import into Unity, the workflow is basically the same as in Unreal, so I believe this process should work smoothly for your project.

comments.author: Pantilieee
comments.body: Hello! How can you create 3d mesh without milions of traingles? In meshy ai, with meshy 6, everything i do (even if it s a car or a part of the car) have 700-800k triangles. When i used remesh in blender all looks ugly and without a strict form. How can you reduce these numbers and also look great? Also, nice work!

replies.author: One_Detective_6143
replies.body: I’ve already used Mesh AI  it will only give you a light mesh if you pay. Rodin AI is more advanced in that area, I think. I tested Mesh AI, Tripo 3D, and Rodin, and for me Rodin stood out the most. It has the option to give you quad meshes, and when the mesh comes in quads, you just need to use the Remesh modifier (being careful not to affect the UV map) and your model is ready. try Rodin ai (hyper 3d)

comments.author: ZealousRealitarian
comments.body: Nine hours for a complete map using AI asset generation is a solid benchmark. The biggest bottleneck right now is usually getting those generated models from Tripo or Rodin into Unreal with correct materials and collision meshes. I am building StudioTwin to handle that exact pipeline step for game dev and virtual production. We automate the cleanup and import process so you never have to leave the editor ;) [studiotwin.ai](http://studiotwin.ai)
